source_base.child_preimage_description: Parent V16 native-formatted postimage, fetched by full Git blob; it is not relabelled as the tested child.

findings: Both complete preimages/postimages were fetched by exact Git blob, byte lengths and SHA256 were independently checked, and all 26 declared edit patterns were applied and reversed with exact occurrence counts.

The registration thread has an explicit anyhow::Result<()> return type, so mapping the join panic into anyhow::Error and then and_then on the inner result is type-consistent with the original two-question-mark propagation.

The original served result is obtained before registration.join. The new failure context retains the already-observed original served debug result alongside the original registration error chain, preventing the old registration-first propagation from hiding that earlier Root result.
Phase already derives Copy and Debug in the fixed parent module, so the added phase labels do not require a new trait or change move/borrow ownership.

The existing assertions, ensure calls, six-phase order, operation calls, TIMEOUT/LIFETIME references and original libc::alarm(60) remain unchanged. Only three fixed stage lines per child phase are added.

The controlled lost-ACK branch still extracts the original AgentdError and passes it directly to the original require_uncertain predicate. The new anyhow context on publish is confined to the branch that expects a successful publication.
The new context wrappers on existing error propagation do not change production code, grants, actual nonce assertions, recovery semantics, denial branches, test selection or the Root parent roster.

No production cause for EAGAIN is established. This change improves subsequent original error evidence only. Shared ChildOwner failure-output retention remains a separate patch and is not certified by this review.
conclusion: No concrete static blocker found in this narrow diagnostic patch. A new fixed-source native attempt is still required; the original 715 failure remains failed.
